A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the local structure and the charge distribution around the Li(+) and OH(-) counterions in microhydrated Li(OH)(n)(H2O)(6-n)(n = 0-6) molecules are probed via the electronic decay of a core-ionization event.
the local environment of an ion in aqueous solution has a significant effect on the electronic decay processes.
the local structure of solvating water molecules and the presence of counterions are reflected on the electronic decays of solvated molecules and ions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

core-ionized states of microhydrated Li(+) and OH(-) ions are not only sensitive to the local structure of the counterion but also to the local structure and the arrangement of solvent molecules in the first solvation shell.
the spectral shape of the core-ionized solute can be used to probe its local hydration structure.
electronic decays in microsolvated ions should be treated in terms of intermolecular charge delocalization.
